newsitem.title: ST LUCIA: St. Lucia banana workers end two-week strike.
newsitem.headline: St. Lucia banana workers end two-week strike.

text.p: Farmers aligned with St. Lucia's Banana Salvation Committee on Monday called off a two-week strike that has crippled the island nation's most important industry.

Abel Wilson, president of the committee, told the Caribbean News Agency it had decided to end what had become a violent work stoppage after weekend talks with a parliamentary committee appointed by Prime Minister Vaughan Lewis.

St. Lucia's government promised that speedy consideration would be given to farmers' grievances over a new carton system, a five-tier payment system and price support. The government also suspended an arrangement that required farmers to pay for their cartons whether or not they used them.
The two-week strike was estimated to have cost St. Lucia's banana industry nearly $1 million.

St. Lucia is in the southeastern Caribbean, with a population of 140,000. It has the largest banana crop in the Windward Islands, producing about 125,000 tons (127,000 tonnes) a year, virtually all for export.
